title: Add and subtract decimals to hundredths by lining up the decimal point

lesson.title: Lining Up the Decimal Point

steps.say: You already know how to add and subtract big numbers in columns, and how to show decimals with grids and blocks. Today we join those two ideas: adding and subtracting decimals right in a column, and the whole secret is where we put the decimal point.

visual.caption: Three point seven five: 3 ones, 7 tenths, 5 hundredths

steps.say: Here is the one rule. Tenths must sit under tenths, hundredths under hundredths, and ones under ones. The easy way to make that happen is to line up the two decimal points one straight under the other, like buttons down the front of a jacket. Why does that work? Because you can only add things that are the same size. Five hundredths and six tenths are different sizes, so they must never share a column.

visual.caption: Two point six: the 6 is tenths, so it belongs in the tenths column

steps.say: Let us buy something. A sandwich costs three dollars and seventy-five cents, and a juice costs two dollars and sixty cents. I write three point seven five, then two point six zero right underneath, decimal point under decimal point. Now I add from the right, just like whole numbers. Five hundredths plus zero hundredths is five hundredths. Seven tenths plus six tenths is thirteen tenths, which is too many, so I regroup: that is one whole and three tenths. I write the three and carry the one. Then three plus two plus that carried one is six. The answer is six dollars and thirty-five cents.

Now here is the mistake I see most often. Some children add one point five plus zero point two five by sliding the numbers to the right edge, so the five in one point five sits under the five hundredths. That gives an answer like zero point four zero, and that cannot be right, because one point five is already bigger than one whole. Remember, the five in one point five means five tenths, not five hundredths. Line up the points instead, and it helps to write one point five as one point five zero. Then five tenths plus two tenths is seven tenths, and zero hundredths plus five hundredths is five hundredths, so the answer is one point seven five.

visual.caption: One point five means 5 tenths — write it as 1.50 to fill the hundredths spot

steps.say: Subtracting works exactly the same way, and we still remember to regroup. Say you have five dollars and you spend one dollar and forty-five cents on a hot chocolate. Write five point zero zero on top and one point four five underneath, points lined up. Zero hundredths take away five hundredths does not work, so I borrow across: five wholes becomes four wholes, nine tenths and ten hundredths. Now ten hundredths minus five hundredths is five hundredths, nine tenths minus four tenths is five tenths, and four minus one is three. You have three dollars and fifty-five cents left.

So whenever you add or subtract decimals, do not look at the right edge — look for the decimal points, stack them straight, fill any empty spots with zeros, and then add or subtract just like you always do.

lesson.answer: Line up the decimal points, fill empty spots with zeros, then add or subtract like whole numbers — and do not forget to regroup.

practice.question: Ms. Yuanyuan's bean sprout was four point five centimetres tall on Monday. By Friday it had grown zero point seven five centimetres more. Write the two numbers in a column with the decimal points lined up (try writing four point five as four point five zero), then add. How tall is the sprout now?
practice.answer: Five point two five centimetres. Lined up, it is 4.50 plus 0.75: zero hundredths plus five hundredths is five hundredths; five tenths plus seven tenths is twelve tenths, so regroup — write two tenths and carry one whole; then four plus zero plus the carried one is five. That gives 5.25 cm.
